technical.summary: Mixed short-term bullish momentum (RSI rising, MACD crossover) conflicted by weak intermediate trend structure (ADX 16.78, EMA 20/50 bearish, price below EMA 50) and stochastic bearish cross; moderate risk/reward for swing entry.

fundamental.summary: ABBV shows no actionable smart money signals with zero insider activity, no institutional positioning data, absent government contracts, no lobbying activity, and minimal retail interest; earnings in 31 days adds timing risk.

sentiment.summary: Extreme fear (15/100) presents contrarian buy opportunity, but mixed congressional activity (2 sales vs 1 purchase, small amounts, junior member) and absent news sentiment provide no confirmation.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds: inverted yield curve signals recession risk, VIX at crisis levels (335.2) indicates extreme market stress, strong dollar pressures multinational healthcare revenues, and earnings in 31 days adds event risk.

debate.key_bull_argument: Short-term momentum (RSI rising, MACD bullish crossover) with extreme fear sentiment (15/100) creates contrarian entry opportunity near support at 122.118.
debate.key_bear_argument: Severe macro headwinds (inverted yield curve, VIX crisis levels, strong dollar), price below EMA 50/Hull MA, weak intermediate trend (ADX 16.78), stochastic bearish cross, and earnings event risk in 31 days outweigh short-term momentum signals.

decision.entry_rationale: Short-term momentum (RSI rising, MACD crossover) and extreme fear sentiment (15/100) create contrarian setup at support. However, severe macro headwinds, weak intermediate trend structure, and earnings event risk in 31 days do not justify entry given portfolio concentration.
decision.primary_risk: Inverted yield curve + VIX crisis levels (335.2) signal systemic stress; earnings in 31 days creates binary event risk with price below EMA 50 and stochastic bearish cross limiting upside confirmation.
decision.agent_agreement: moderate — technical shows short-term bullish signals but fundamental, sentiment, and risk agents all flag severe macro and event headwinds; debate decisively favors bear case.
